correctness.rationale: For every named strict chain of length n>=0 in the Fraisse limit of posets with a linear extension, finite diagrams exhaust complete injective tuple types. After fixing the coordinate linear orientation and gaps 0<=i<=j<=n, lower/upper cuts determine all old-new comparisons. For x below y in the partial order, exactly the lower-cut and upper-cut monotonicity inequalities are necessary and sufficient for transitivity; for x,y incomparable, exactly the condition u_x>ell_y excludes the sole possible old-vertex two-step witness. This establishes the two explicit double sums for C_n and I_n. Each polynomial summand has total degree <=4 with integral linear bounds; two summations produce a polynomial in n of degree <=6, making agreement at n=0,...,6 a rigorous all-n identity rather than a finite extrapolation. Rational algebra yields the strictly decreasing 5/14 comparable fraction and the 7/5 ratio to the squared unary count. The independent all-diagram transitivity enumerator checks n=0,...,7, exact sum checks n=0,...,16. The standalone checker in verification/check_lo_poset.py was executed; verification/output.txt contains actual success output. No finite run is substituted for the polynomial-degree proof.

originality.rationale: The base object and homogeneous extension property were introduced in foundational literature, while the closest published chain-base tuple-type order-polynomial formula concerns the reduct without its distinguished linear extension. Consequently its quartic scalar pair polynomial does not imply the ordered-expansion's sextic, partial-order-channel-refined spectrum. An earlier ordered-poset calculation over named antichains concerns exponentially many extensions and does not imply the chain count. The comparable channel alone coincides numerically with the previously tabulated Narayana-derived OEIS A006542; that numerical sequence is acknowledged rather than claimed as new. The joint structural interpretation, exact incomparable channel, and strictly decreasing comparability fraction with 5/14 limit were not located in inspected sources after actual searches. Best-knowledge originality only; unindexed equivalent order-polynomial derivations remain possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical paper may compute the same pair-channel count under linear-extension or order-polynomial terminology.
Comparable-channel numbers themselves are an existing sequence; novelty is specifically the joint model-theoretic formula and distribution law, not the integers.
Only publicly accessible portions of Sokic's Ramsey paper were examined; its uninspected sections cannot be ruled out exhaustively.

value.rationale: Pointwise named finite chains are a canonical family for extensions of the generic linearly ordered poset. The finding separates partial-order comparabilities from incomparabilities within a fixed linear extension and gives complete exact rational-polynomial formulas for both, rather than a single unmotivated coefficient. The strictly decreasing comparable fraction from 1/2 to 5/14 reveals a substantive boundary effect; the limit differs from 1/2 for the reduct's chain-base two-types and 3/7 for ordered antichain bases. The exact 7/5 ratio to squared unary types calibrates asymptotic correlations of two new logical coordinates. Claims are confined to motivated base and arity scopes; no unsupported arbitrary-poset or higher-arity extension is asserted.
